nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Education on responsible consumption
nodes.label: Education on responsible consumption

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Education on responsible consumption_qna_000
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How does education influence consumer behaviour towards sustainable products?
nodes.answer: Education directly influences knowledge levels, which, in turn, can impact consumer choices towards sustainable products, as seen in various studies.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Education on responsible consumption_qna_001
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How did education initially influence the intention to purchase environmentally friendly products, and what was the long-term effect?
nodes.answer: Education initially fostered the intention to consume more environmentally friendly products, but this change did not persist over time and did not lead to behaviour change (Frolic et al., 2013).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Education on responsible consumption_qna_002
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why is it emphasized that educating consumers alone is not sufficient for achieving a sustainable shift in food consumption?
nodes.answer: While educating consumers is essential, it is noted that a sustainable shift in consumption requires the combination of various policy instruments beyond consumer education.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Education on responsible consumption_qna_003
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What percentage of respondents with a high education level correctly perceive where the largest share of environmental impacts of Swiss consumption accrues?
nodes.answer: 50% of respondents with a high education level correctly perceive that the largest share of environmental impacts of Swiss consumption primarily accrues abroad.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Education on responsible consumption_qna_004
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the aim of CE consumption policies in relation to consumer behaviour?
nodes.answer: CE consumption policies aim to promote the consumption of CE-compatible products by influencing consumers both obligatorily and informatively.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Education on responsible consumption_qna_005
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can digital technologies be used to promote sustainable consumption among customers?
nodes.answer: Digital technologies can be used to communicate and interact with customers directly, aiding in promoting sustainable consumption education and instilling a sense of responsibility in consumers.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Education on responsible consumption_qna_006
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can digital technologies help in promoting sustainable consumption education?
nodes.answer: Digital technologies can aid in promoting sustainable consumption education by using app-based communication to interact with customers directly and instilling a sense of responsibility in consumers.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Education on responsible consumption_qna_007
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How do consumers primarily become aware of environmental care practices in stores?
nodes.answer: The vast majority of consumers, 67.7%, stated that they knew about environmental care practices when they were inside the store. 51.6% said it was through the internet, and 16.1% got the information from their families.
